translation:
  text: 'I say to him, “Sir, make known to me what this tree is; for I am perplexed about it, because,
    though so many branches have been cut off, the tree is sound, and nothing appears to have been cut
    away from it. About this, therefore, I am at a loss.”


    “Listen,” he says. “This great tree that covers plains and mountains and the whole earth is the law
    of God given to the whole world. And this law is the Son of God, proclaimed to the ends of the earth;
    and the peoples under the shade are those who heard the proclamation and believed in him.[a]


    “And the great and glorious angel is Michael, who has authority over this people and governs them.
    For he is the one who gives the law to them, into the hearts of those who believe; therefore he himself
    visits those to whom he gave it, to see whether they have kept it.


    “You see the rods of each person; for the rods are the law. You see, then, many rods made worthless;
    and you will recognize all those who have not kept the law, and you will see the dwelling of each
    one.”[b][c]


    I say to him, “Sir, why did he send some away into the tower, but leave others to you?”


    “All who transgressed the law which they received from him,” he says, “he left under my authority
    for repentance[i]; but those who have already been pleasing to the law and have kept it, he has under
    his own authority.”[d][e]


    “Who then, Sir,” I say, “are the ones who are crowned and go into the tower?”


    “[Those who grappled with the devil and overcame him,” he says, “are crowned.][f][g] These are the
    ones who suffered for the law.[h]


    “But the others, who themselves also handed in their rods green and having side-shoots, yet without
    fruit—these are those who were hard-pressed for the law, but did not suffer, nor did they deny their
    law.


    “And those who handed in green rods just as they received them are dignified and righteous and have
    walked with a very pure heart, and have guarded the commandments of the Lord. The rest you will learn
    when I examine these rods that have been planted and watered.”'

  - marker: b

    reason: cross_reference
  - marker: c

translation:
  text: 'I say to him, “Sir, explain what this tree is. I do not understand how so many branches could
    be cut off while the tree remains whole, with no sign that anything was removed. That is why I am
    puzzled.”


    “Listen,” he said. “This great tree, whose shade covers the plains, the mountains, and the whole earth,
    is God’s law, given to the whole world. This law is the Son of God, who has been proclaimed to the
    ends of the earth. The peoples under the tree’s shade are those who heard the message and believed
    in him.[a]


    “The great and glorious angel is Michael. He has authority over this people and governs them. For
    he gives the law to those who believe, putting it in their hearts. So he himself visits those to whom
    he gave it to see whether they have obeyed it.


    “The rods you see belong to different people, and they stand for the law.[b] You see that many of
    the rods have become useless.[c] In this way, you will recognize all who have not obeyed the law,
    and you will see each person’s dwelling place.”


    I asked him, “Sir, why did he send some into the tower but leave the others with you?”


    He says, “He placed under my authority all who broke the law they received from him, so that they
    could repent[d][i]. But he keeps under his own authority those who have already lived in a way pleasing
    to the law and have kept it.”[e]


    I asked, “Then who are the people wearing crowns and entering the tower, sir?”


    “[Those who struggled against the devil and defeated him,” he says, “are crowned.][f][g] They are
    the ones who suffered for the law.[h]


    “The others themselves also returned their rods green, with side shoots but no fruit. They are those
    who came under pressure because of the law, but did not actually suffer or deny their law.


    “Those who returned their rods as green as when they received them are honorable and righteous. They
    have lived with very pure hearts and have kept the Lord’s commandments. You will learn about the others
    when I examine the rods that were planted and watered.”'

  - marker: b

base_translation:
  text: 'I say to him, “Sir, make known to me what this tree is; for I am perplexed about it, because,
    though so many branches have been cut off, the tree is sound, and nothing appears to have been cut
    away from it. About this, therefore, I am at a loss.”


    “Listen,” he says. “This great tree that covers plains and mountains and the whole earth is the law
    of God given to the whole world. And this law is the Son of God, proclaimed to the ends of the earth;
    and the peoples under the shade are those who heard the proclamation and believed in him.[a]


    “And the great and glorious angel is Michael, who has authority over this people and governs them.
    For he is the one who gives the law to them, into the hearts of those who believe; therefore he himself
    visits those to whom he gave it, to see whether they have kept it.


    “You see the rods of each person; for the rods are the law. You see, then, many rods made worthless;
    and you will recognize all those who have not kept the law, and you will see the dwelling of each
    one.”[b][c]


    I say to him, “Sir, why did he send some away into the tower, but leave others to you?”


    “All who transgressed the law which they received from him,” he says, “he left under my authority
    for repentance[i]; but those who have already been pleasing to the law and have kept it, he has under
    his own authority.”[d][e]


    “Who then, Sir,” I say, “are the ones who are crowned and go into the tower?”


    “[Those who grappled with the devil and overcame him,” he says, “are crowned.][f][g] These are the
    ones who suffered for the law.[h]


    “But the others, who themselves also handed in their rods green and having side-shoots, yet without
    fruit—these are those who were hard-pressed for the law, but did not suffer, nor did they deny their
    law.


    “And those who handed in green rods just as they received them are dignified and righteous and have
    walked with a very pure heart, and have guarded the commandments of the Lord. The rest you will learn
    when I examine these rods that have been planted and watered.”'
